discussion_comments.comment_body: Does this map to https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/session-info-update or something custom? I am trying to figure out if this is modifying an extended type or an object which should be representing the type from ACP-mainline.

oh yea, it's a Goose-internal type, not the ACP wire format, activeRunId already follows this same pattern : https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/main/ui/desktop/src/acp/adapter/shared.ts#L12 ,  `gooseMode` is the same idea, sourced from the standard ACP `current_mode_update`

The main purpose of this PR is to make the backend-persisted `session.name` the single source of truth for displayed session names. Recipe sessions now start the same way as normal sessions, with the initial default name.  Once the first reply happens, `maybe_update_name()` sees the attached recipe and persists `recipe.title` into `session.name`. From then on, UI/ACP surfaces display that backend-owned name.

I don’t think we should restore the frontend `session.recipe.title` fallback here because that would move display name logic back into the client.

I addressed this by removing the desktop import/use of `GooseInitializeRequest` instead of restoring the SDK export.

`GooseInitializeRequest` was only used as a TypeScript `satisfies` check at the desktop call site; it has no runtime behavior, and`GooseClient.initialize(...)` already type-checks its argument via the ACP `InitializeRequest` method signature. 

Since the SDK is still early and we do not want a separate initialize request type that can drift from the actual method contract, I think avoiding this exported type is the cleaner fix.

This is intentional. `_goose/unstable/session/update` has its own typed callback, `unstable_sessionUpdate`, which is how consumers are meant to receive it. extNotification is just the fallback for methods that don't have a typed callback . 

Consumer can get the notification and implement the callback.

These methods stand out to me as repeating what the client already offers with only slightly different signatures/naming. Is the goal to make something that makes it so each calling location in the client doesn't need to manage `const client = await getAcpClient()` ?

If so, I wonder if the right approach is to make a react hook version of `GooseClient`, expose it from the SDK, and use that everywhere? This would eliminate the duplication.

cc @jamadeo for thoughts too
a hook version of GooseClient sounds great 👍
